note: Expected animation fidelity for the nine cases that pin the pivot / 3D animation contract. Consumed by test/run_html_anim_eval.sh (and by test/run_html_eval.sh when HTML_ANIM_EVAL=1). A case whose ssimMean falls more than `tolerance` below its `ssim` fails the run; a higher score is only reported, because it means the ledger is stale.
toleranceRule: 0.005 for the cases above 0.99 (they only differ from the baseline by browser anti-aliasing), 0.02 for 49_rotate3d_depth_pivot, whose baseline still differs by ~3% of pixels and is therefore the noisiest row.

cases.note: 2D rotate() about an off-centre transform-origin stays on the `matrix` channel; the pivot must not move the shape.
2D scale() about an off-centre pivot keeps the same routing as rotate(), with the pivot applied once by the runtime.
A rotate3d()/rotateY() track about the box centre rides the `matrix3D` channel; keyframes stay un-pivoted.
3D rotation about an off-centre pivot: the pivot lands on `Layer.anchor`, not inside the keyframe matrices.
An animated text leaf routes its pivot through the host layer, so the text must not drift while it rotates.
An inline-SVG shape keeps its structural pivot (the generated group position) instead of `Layer.anchor`.
A pivot with depth (transform-origin z) cannot move to the parent-camera form; the camera skip is expected (cameraSkips: depth-pivot), so this row is bounded below 1.0.
Parent `perspective` is folded into the child pose; a 2D animation under it must not gain a projection row.
An inline-SVG shape animation ignores the parent camera, which is lossless while shape poses stay on the z = 0 plane (see 13.7).
